meta.description: Memory recall hook + router shadow mode

user.t:
You are hive agent "loop-closer" (a ruflo coder). Read C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md, BUS.md (latest entries), sona-trainer's results (C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/bench/RULE.md, bench/results/) and llm-smith.md. Repo: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh (ingest/ is Python, the mesh CLI is target/release/neural-mesh.exe; build with ~/.cargo/bin/cargo.exe plus the WinLibs mingw PATH, because `cargo` on PATH is an npm shim). The user approved both features below. Build them opt-in, measure them, and hand the hook config to the queen. Do NOT edit ~/.claude/settings.json yourself.

1) MEMORY RECALL HOOK (Claude Code UserPromptSubmit; stdout is injected into the model context)
- Script: neural-mesh/hooks/recall_hook.py (or a fast compiled path).
- It reads the hook JSON from stdin (prompt, cwd, session_id).
- It decides whether the prompt is about the user's code or projects (repo identifiers, file paths, project names, conventions). Use a cheap gate (regex/keywords, plus a lexical/BM25 or MiniLM score threshold) and skip everything else.
- It calls the ingest MemoryStore recall (top-k ≤ 3, logged for usefulness credit with the session id) and prints a short block, ≤ 600 tokens, of memories that pass a relevance floor. When nothing passes, it prints nothing.
- Hard limits:
  - total wall time ≤ 1.5 s (budget it; on timeout print nothing);
  - never print secrets (re-run ingest's scrubber on the output);
  - never fail the turn (always exit 0);
  - toggle with env NEURAL_MESH_RECALL=off.
- Measure:
  - (a) latency p50/p95 over 50 real prompts from transcripts;
  - (b) the fire rate on the last ~300 real user prompts, and how many tokens it adds on average;
  - (c) answer quality, using sona-trainer's bench (bench/run.py, battery.json): run condition B with your hook's exact gate+recall as the front-end vs A (Claude alone), on the full battery. Report the paired CI per category and tokens. Use haiku-4-5 via `claude -p` exactly as bench/run.py does; keep MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=2048; budget ≤ 2 runs.
- Keep the hook only if accuracy is not worse outside the private-repo items (TOST ±.03) and it helps on them.

2) ROUTER SHADOW MODE (agent suggestion next to the fixed rule)
- A PreToolUse hook on Task|Agent: neural-mesh/hooks/route_shadow.py.
- It asks `neural-mesh route` for its pick, given the dispatch's description/prompt features, with the candidates = the subagent types seen in the router state.
- It also computes the fixed phase-rule pick (reuse the router-eval rule from scratchpad/router-eval/).
- It logs {ts, session, actual subagent_type, mesh_pick, rule_pick} to data/lifelong/route_shadow.jsonl.
- It prints NOTHING and never blocks.
- Add `python -m ingest shadow-report`: rolling accuracy of mesh vs rule against the actual choice, with a Wilson CI and n.
- Add an explicit promotion rule (do NOT turn it on): when the mesh beats the rule with the CI lower bound > the rule's over ≥ 100 shadow dispatches, the report says "ELIGIBLE". Only then can the queen let the hook print a one-line suggestion.
- Make sure the nightly ingest feeds the router with the actual choice as a label (`feedback --label`), with env failures as `--failure-class env`, consistent with mesh-coder's R117-R121.

Shared rules:
- Hooks must cost ≤ 50 ms when disabled and must be robust on Windows (python startup cost: measure it; if the recall p95 is over 1.5 s, use a persistent local helper or the Rust binary instead).
- Tests: Python unit tests for the gating, the scrub-on-output, the timeout, and silence on error.
- Commit to neural-mesh master by explicit path, local only.
- Write hooks/settings-hooks-recall.json with the exact entries for the queen to merge. Use timeouts that are safe: the recall hook's Claude Code timeout must exceed its internal budget.
- Return ≤ 30 lines: numbers, verdicts, commits, and the hook JSON path.

handback.t:
loop-closer report (neural-mesh master, local only; my commit 5dcb5c6, plus my earlier files that the owner's WIP commit bfb50fe swept up: recall_hook.py, memory.py log_retrieval, bench/run.py hook switch)

HOOK CONFIG: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/hooks/settings-hooks-recall.json (UserPromptSubmit recall, timeout 3 s over a 1.2 s internal budget; PreToolUse "Task|Agent" shadow, timeout 8 s over 2.5 s). Absolute python.exe with -S. I did not touch ~/.claude/settings.json. Details: hooks/README.md.

1) RECALL HOOK (hooks/recall_hook.py): built, measured, NOT shown to help. Do not rely on it. Merge only the PreToolUse block unless you want it anyway; it is safe either way (silent unless confident, exit 0 always).
- Latency (python -S, end to end): 50 real prompts p50 86-100 ms, p95 123-145 ms (3 runs); worst case (all gate-passing, 194-memory pool) p50 109-120, p95 144-163, max 182 ms. Python startup is ~35 ms, so no Rust/helper needed. Disabled (env off): p50 37-38 ms, p95 39-40 ms.
- Scaling: about 75 us per memory in the pool, so past ~15k memories in one project the 1.2 s budget fires and the hook goes silent.
- Fire rate on real prompts: only 207 exist (<300; scrubbed, 2026-10-03..10). Gate passes 37%, but it fires 0/207 as typed (0 tokens added). If every prompt were typed inside neural-mesh it fires 3/207 (1.4%), ~88 est. tokens each (chars/4). Unscoped across projects it fired 22% at an earlier threshold, but the hits were off-topic.
- Battery (MESH_FRONTEND=hook python bench/run.py --cond A,B --tag hook1, n=120, haiku-4-5, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=2048, 1 run of the 2 allowed): the hook fired on 1/120 prompts and 0/15 private items.
  - Overall B-A -0.008 [-0.042,+0.017]; excl. private -0.009 [-0.048,+0.019], 90% CI [-0.038,+0.019], so TOST +-.03 is NOT met; private 0.00 -> 0.00 (CI [0,0]); tokens -11 [-55,+49].
  - On 119/120 prompts B received the identical prompt, so that difference is haiku replicate noise (1 win, 2 losses). Per category, math -0.033 [-0.167,+0.067], research:public 0.000, code 0.000, physics 0.000.
- Verdict by your rule (equivalence off private AND a gain on private): KEEP=false. Cause: none of the 606 memories contains the private constants (they live in src/*.rs), and real prompts are mostly directives, so the memory store rarely matches. The BM25 repo front-end (0.00 -> 1.00) is the tool for those facts, not this hook.
- Tests: 18 unit tests (gate, project scoping, scrub-on-output including a secret and PII, only injected memories logged with the session id, timeout, silence on garbage/corrupt/missing store, env off). I mutation-checked that they fail when scrub or the floor is broken.

2) ROUTER SHADOW (hooks/route_shadow.py, python -m ingest shadow-report): built, NOT turned on beyond logging.
- Hook logs {ts, session, tool_use_id, actual, mesh_pick, rule_pick, n_cand, mesh_ms} to data/lifelong/route_shadow.jsonl and prints nothing. It costs ~220 ms per dispatch. It routes on a temp COPY of the state: the current neural-mesh.exe `route` mutates counters in the state file (calls, routes, teams_routed, team_size_sum). One of my probes ran `route` on the live state before I found this and bumped those counters once.
- shadow-report: Wilson 95% CIs, McNemar, rolling window. Rule (fr-* roster) and the explicit promotion rule: ELIGIBLE iff >= 100 in-domain (actual is fr-*) shadow dispatches AND the mesh's Wilson lower bound > the rule's accuracy. Currently NOT ELIGIBLE (0 logged).
- Nightly feed (ingest/meshio.py): `feedback --label <actual agent>`; env failures (turn_limit / redispatch_cue / api_error on a re-dispatch) as `--agent X --reward 0 --failure-class env` (30 of 550 outcomes); INGEST_MESH_FEED=reward restores the old feed; a binary that rejects the new flags falls back to the legacy feed per event so nothing is lost.
- Finding: the live router state is weak. For a review task the mesh picked ruflo-plugin-creator:plugin-developer. Offline `python -m ingest rebuild-router --dry-run --eval` (label-fed replay of 550 outcomes, candidates = all agents seen so far) gives prequential 57.2% over all dispatches (below the 75% general-purpose majority). On the 25 fr-* dispatches the mesh scores 24% vs the phase rule's 84% (the rule's keywords were written after seeing the data, so optimistic). Expect NOT ELIGIBLE for a long time. I did NOT run the rebuild live: someone else just merged the live state (router_state.json.pre-merge.20261010-065031), and the rebuild would overwrite it (it backs up first, so it is reversible). Your call.
- Tests: ingest/tests/test_shadow.py and hooks/tests/test_route_shadow.py (rule, Wilson, McNemar, promotion boundaries, feed policy against the real binary, stale-binary fallback, state hash unchanged, silence on garbage/missing binary/zero budget/unwritable log). 73 tests pass in total with the existing ingest suites.

Other notes: target/release/neural-mesh.exe was stale (rejected --label and --failure-class) until someone rebuilt it at 06:50; it now accepts them. My temp worktree and target dir are removed. Not mine and untouched: ingest/mirror.py, llm/README.md.
